newsitem.title: ANTIGUA: CRICKET-INDIAN BOWLERS MAKE UP FOR LOST TIME.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIAN BOWLERS MAKE UP FOR LOST TIME.

text.p: India did their best to inject some interest into the rain-ruined fourth test against West Indies by taking three wickets before lunch in the first session of play permitted by the weather.

After three days without a ball bowled, the match finally started on the fourth morning beneath clear blue skies but none of the West Indian batsmen looked comfortable after Courtney Walsh had won the delayed toss.

Stuart Williams departed for a duck, caught at slip to a poor shot outside off-stump against Abey Kuruvilla, and fellow opener Sherwin Campbell was run out for 10 by a superb one-handed pick-up and direct hit from Ajay Jadeja in the covers.

Shivnarine Chanderpaul dug in in characteristic fashion for 24 before offering a bat-pad chance to short-leg off Anil Kumble to leave his side on 40 for three, but Carl Hooper and Brian Lara took the home side through to lunch without further loss.
Hooper was on 13 and Lara on eight as West Indies reached the interval on 62 for three.
